argument_summary: The supportable position on the present admissible record is narrower than clean certification. The evidence supports launch readiness at an aggregate level because the release clears aggregate launch readiness by 2.0 percentage points, has no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and passes general support, latency, and rollback checks. The same record also shows that privilege-sensitive matter routing is a named deployment context with queued evaluations that are not in the packet, and QA characterizes that area as unknown rather than passed. The right audit treatment is therefore to distinguish aggregate operational readiness from context-specific validation: certification can be defended only if treated as caveated and tied to explicit disclosure of that unresolved named-context evaluation gap, not as a no-limitation validation of the routing context.
claims_about_business_cost: No independent business-cost claim is needed to resolve the audit question. The supportable request is based on risk-weighted interpretation of the admissible policy and evaluation record, not on side-channel launch pressure.
claims_about_policy: The policy text is the main constraint. It says model-card certification must disclose material limitations and evaluation gaps for named deployment contexts, and that passing general benchmarks and load tests can support launch readiness but missing evaluation coverage for named customer contexts must be disclosed or resolved before clean certification. On this record, aggregate readiness evidence supports a readiness claim, but it does not support clean no-limitation certification for privilege-sensitive matter routing. Public model-card guidance and AI risk-management guidance are consistent with that reading because they support documenting limitations, evaluation results, and ongoing risk management across deployment.
concessions: The present record does not show that the final model card or certification packet already contains the required disclosure text.
The present record does not support treating privilege-sensitive matter routing as validated or passed.
The present record does not support clean no-limitation certification for the named routing context.
If required disclosure is absent from the final certification materials, the compliance case weakens materially.
